findings.title: Couldn't confirm: VOC (air quality)
findings.detail: VOC lower than SCAQMD 1168 requires (250 g/L: the Rule 1168 architectural sealant limit; the number comes from the rule, not the spec).
findings.why_it_matters: Without confirmed low VOC levels, we can’t ensure indoor air quality meets environmental rules during occupancy.

findings.title: Couldn't confirm: astm g21 rating
findings.detail: Firestopping materials shall have mold and mildew resistance rating of zero(0) in accordance with ASTM G21.
findings.why_it_matters: Mold resistance is needed in damp areas to prevent long-term material breakdown and health risks.

findings.title: Couldn't compare: Temperature rating (T)
findings.detail: Values were not comparable.
findings.why_it_matters: If the T-rating isn’t sufficient, heat could transfer through the seal during a fire, risking flame spread on the unexposed side.

findings.title: Couldn't confirm: Test standards
findings.detail: Tested in accordance with ASTM E814, ASTM E119 or UL 1479.
findings.why_it_matters: Using the wrong test standard means we can’t trust the firestop will perform as expected in a real fire.

findings.title: Does not meet: Pipe types covered
findings.detail: Package lists PVC, ABS, FRPP, CPVC, PVDF, PEX; needs steel pipe.
findings.why_it_matters: The product doesn’t cover steel pipe, so using it here would leave a gap that fails to stop fire or smoke.
